report: Fever, left shoulder pain, pericardial effusion, reduced cardiac sounds, and tachycardia three weeks after an upper respiratory infection, with neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated CRP/ESR, and ECG PR depression/ST elevation, indicate bacterial pericarditis. Negative TB, viral, and ANA tests and no arthralgia/abdominal pain exclude tuberculous, viral, systemic inflammatory, and drug causes. Specialists concur; pending cultures limit confidence to 0.65, but bacterial pericarditis is most likely.
